 'Very interesting': Trump suggests recent gas price drops are linked to the election
 Ben Werschkul · Washington Correspondent Fri, November 20, 2026 at 1:34 PM CST 2 min read PFE -0.36%

 Learn more President Trump on Friday escalated a suggestion he has been making on social media that the recent dip in energy prices is being driven by political forces now that the midterm election is in the rearview mirror. 
 "Crude oil prices have plummeted right since the end of the election: I wonder how that happened?" Trump said during a press conference to discuss this week's trip to Asia . "Too bad we didn't have that in front of the election, but that's the way it goes." 
 The president then made his insinuation more direct, comparing the price drop to the time Pfizer's ( PFE ) COVID vaccine was unveiled days after the 2020 election. 
 "I know the system," Trump said about the recent gas price decline. "Let's not call it corrupt, let's call it very interesting." 
 President Donald Trump speaks as Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio look on during a news briefing at the the White House on November 20. (Alex Wong/Getty Images) · Alex Wong via Getty Images The remarks were an escalation of a claim Trump has been making on Truth Social over the last week , though there is no clear evidence that global energy markets have shifted in recent weeks based on US political factors . 
 The most recent figures from AAA show the national average gas price is now below $3.70 per gallon, the lowest since March, soon after the War in Iran began. 
 "Many will assume the election had something to do with it, but that's a myth," said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, in a recent newsletter. Seasonal factors and more oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz are more important, he wrote. 
 Read more:  How oil price shocks ripple through your wallet, from gas to groceries 
 Gas prices have also historically declined in the fall after the summer driving season, due to a variety of factors. 
 At another point during Friday's press conference, Trump said crude oil prices had gone up less than he thought; he had expected them to top $300 a barrel after hostilities in Iran began. 
 Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.
